nodes.label: org-001 the program encodes status into durable artifactory directory names: one name announces a worker beacon and another announces completion plus a result-chunk count.
org-002 the payload reads an artifactory mailbox directory and packages the retrieved text into a repository file named boardtest.txt.
org-003 the recovered nested program lists a mailbox directory, orders numbered name fragments, reconstructs a compressed payload, and treats the result as executable input.
org-004 the artifact explicitly attributes a template used by the enclosed program to a named shared board.
org-005 a long-running loop reads a remote request log, extracts command-shaped urls, executes each unseen request, posts keyed results, and periodically emits a beat.
org-006 when the request log reaches a threshold, the program creates a replacement channel token, announces the rotation through the old channel, and resets local deduplication state.
org-007 the receiver dispatches each unseen command id to a separate worker thread while retaining a shared seen set and heartbeat.
org-008 the controller polls a repository file, hashes its contents to suppress immediate repeats, executes changed content, and commits an output file to the same repository.
org-009 the program polls cmd.json for three hours and executes a command only when its sequence differs and its signature verifies over the sequence, timeout, and command.
org-010 the program creates an exclusive local marker, exits if it already exists, and rewrites the repository trigger into an inert completion state.
org-011 closely related retained variants use an exclusive worker marker, a non-main output branch, trigger neutralization, and a bounded authenticated follow-up loop.
org-012 on startup, the program reads a pid from a worker-local lock, exits if that process is alive, and otherwise overwrites the lock with its own pid before polling signed commands.
org-013 several copies could attempt the same exclusive creation on a shared filesystem; the copy that creates the lock continues and any copy seeing an existing lock exits.
org-014 the g23619 program repeatedly reads one repository command file, decodes a numbered command, executes it, and commits encrypted output under a command-labelled filename.
org-015 the command number and compressed body are hashed and checked against an embedded rsa public key before decompression and execution.
org-016 processed command numbers are loaded from and written back to a local seen file; a number already in that set is skipped.

org-017 each copy reads the current repository revision and attempts a conditional commit containing its claim while neutralizing the launch configuration; a revision conflict makes the losing copy exit.
org-018 the controller periodically publishes encrypted heartbeat state containing its host, pid, processed commands, and error count, then publishes an exit record.
org-019 the payload constructs a repository commit that restores the g23619 launch configuration after the controller's claim path had been designed to neutralize it.
org-020 the archive contains twenty-eight decoded signed command artifacts: eighteen records for the main command file because number 000007 has two bodies, and ten for the child command file.
org-021 the archive contains two different signed command bodies with the same six-digit command number, while the controller deduplicates solely on that number.
org-022 a signed main-channel command contains a decoded child controller that uses a separate command file, output namespace, seen file, and heartbeat loop.
org-023 the libr11 controller claims an exclusive local lock, polls c2cmd.json for six hours, accepts only a valid hmac, and suppresses repeats by the hash of the full command object.
org-024 copies sharing the filesystem attempt the same atomic directory creation; the successful copy declares itself leader and a losing copy terminates its parent controller.

org-025 future9180 variant v1 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.

org-026 future9180 variant v2 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.

org-027 future9180 variant v3 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.

org-028 future9180 variant v4 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.

org-029 future9180 variant v6 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.

org-030 future9180 variant v8 deletes a lock older than thirty minutes, exclusively creates the replacement lock, refreshes its timestamp while polling, and accepts only increasing signed command numbers.
org-031 the ots92 program uses one repository discussion as both an inbound command board and an outbound heartbeat, result, and completion board.
org-032 the command compares the current hostname to an explicit keep-list and terminates the ots92 controller everywhere else.
org-033 the installer terminates earlier sc4tiny processes, writes a replacement controller under a new path and channel prefix, and launches it detached.

org-034 each be90 instance generates a fresh symmetric key and identifier, publishes a public-key-wrapped handshake, accepts only hmac-valid commands addressed to its prefix, deduplicates command hashes, and publishes encrypted results.
org-035 the helper uses an isolated non-main branch for addressed command files and encrypted result files, rejects invalid or repeated command bodies, and supports an authenticated stop instruction.

org-036 the program first disarms its active launch configuration, then polls cmd66.json on an inactive branch for increasing hmac-authenticated sequence numbers and emits results back to that branch.

org-037 two private-control source families explicitly describe remote execution or upload as gated on a later coordination signal; their code operationalizes that boundary through addressed authenticated commands.
